paper_summary: Hybrid syntactic foams were made by hand lay-up casting of K20 hollow glass microballoons and fly ash cenospheres into a DGEBA-based vinyl ester matrix (MEKP hardener), at two total filler loadings (50 and 60 vol%) with the internal glass:cenosphere ratio varied in 25 vol% steps. Unnotched Izod impact (ASTM D256) and three-point flexure (ASTM D790) were measured. Increasing cenosphere content raised flexural modulus and, in most cases, flexural strength; the maximum reported gains were 111% in impact strength and 39%/58% in flexural strength/modulus relative to the all-glass-microballoon foam, while matrix porosity stayed in the 7-10% range.

extraction_notes: Only five absolute property values are stated numerically in this paper; everything else appears solely in unlabelled bar charts (Fig. 1 density/porosity, Figs. 2 and 6 impact strength, Figs. 9-10 and 12-13 flexural strength/modulus) and was therefore left null per rule 2. The six hybrid compositions (50/60HSF-75-25, -50-50, -25-75) were NOT emitted as records: the paper reports them only as percentage changes relative to the all-glass foam (e.g. '-23, 1.4% and 9%' for the 50% series, '18%, 9% and 39%' for the 60% series), and back-computing absolute strengths from those percentages would be a derived, not a stated, number. Flexural modulus is likewise only given as percentage change with no stated absolute baseline, so modulus_mpa is null for every record. Impact results (unnotched Izod, ASTM D256-02) are reported in J/m and J-m2/kg, units with no corresponding schema field, so no impact records were created; the qualitative findings are captured in paper_summary. Filler is a two-particle hybrid but particle_type is a single enum, so only the plain (single-filler) compositions are represented here and particle_volume_fraction is the TOTAL filler volume fraction (0.50 or 0.60). K20 particle_true_density_g_cc is entered as 0.20 g/cm3, the midpoint of the manufacturer's 0.18-0.22 g/cm3 true-density range (Table I); mean diameter 60 um is the 50th-percentile size. Cenosphere true density (0.6-0.8 g/cc) and size ('<300 microns') are ranges only and were left null. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 72 C is the post-cure temperature (3 h at 72 C after ~20 h room-temperature cure). Test temperature was not stated and is assumed room temperature (25 C). The neat-resin flexural strength of 104 MPa is marked data_origin=secondary because the paper attributes it to ref [17] (Tagliavia, Porfiri & Gupta 2010); its particle_type entry is a schema placeholder since the sample contains no particles (particle_volume_fraction = 0). Note the paper cites ASTM D256-02 in the text but lists ASTM D6110-10 (Charpy) as ref [13], an internal inconsistency.
